The boundary rule · six extension mechanisms

Six extension mechanisms.
Zero modifications to Payment Base core.

The boundary rule

If it could work with another PSP — it lives in payment-component.

If it touches \Stripe\StripeClient or PayPal SDK concepts — it lives in the PSP module.

PayPal and Stripe are peers. They share only Payment Base. Architecture grep guards in each PSP’s pre-commit-check.sh block any cross-import.

File layout convention
extensions/your-psp/
├── src/
│   ├── Adapter/        # YourPspAdapter
│   ├── EventSystem/
│   │   ├── Event/      # YourPsp...RequestEvent
│   │   └── Handler/    # YourPsp...Handler
│   ├── Service/        # YourPsp business services
│   └── Webhook/        # YourPspWebhookProcessor
├── services.yaml       # the wiring
└── tests/Unit + Integration
Six mechanisms · pick the smallest one that fits
1
Event Handler
Subscribe to a contract / payment event. The default extension point.
Low
2
Service Override via DI
Replace or decorate a service binding in services.yaml. Inheritance + Symfony aliasing.
Medium
3
Contract Metadata
Store custom data on a contract via setMetadata(). Survives the lifecycle.
Low
4
Webhook Handler Addition
Handle a new PSP webhook event type. Extends AbstractWebhookProcessor.
Medium
5
Controller Extension
Add UI or logic to existing checkout / admin pages. Use only for thin orchestration.
Medium
6
Adapter Decoration
Wrap StripeAdapter / PayPalAdapter for marketplace headers, logging, retries.
High
